title: spec(dashboard): a globalFilters entry named `dateRange` parses and silently replaces the built-in date range's binding
body:
domain:spec#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmPi25XXKx92Xmg4viS

Filing gate: ① a defect named out of scope by the #29023 implementer (os-dev-report 6572629846, out_of_scope_findings[0]). ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it. Reach is NOT MEASURED at a public door: the parse accepts it, and lint's `dashboardFilterDefs` lets the later definition win.

## What happens

- `GlobalFilterSchema.name` says `dateRange` is reserved for the built-in date range, and the widget `filterBindings` describe in `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` (≈L1389–1404 on main) keys the built-in filter as `dateRange` when the dashboard declares `dateRange`.
- A dashboard that declares `dateRange` AND a `globalFilters` entry named `dateRange` parses. Lint's `dashboardFilterDefs` keeps the later definition, so the entry silently replaces the built-in filter's binding. An author reads a date-range control that filters some other field.
- PR #29162 (#29023) refuses two `globalFilters` entries under one key, but `dateRange` is not a `globalFilters` entry, so this collision is outside that refusal.

## Wanted

Measure it at the save door and on the console board first. If it reproduces, refuse a `globalFilters` entry keyed `dateRange` (by name, or by field when unnamed) on a dashboard that declares `dateRange`, naming the reserved word. That is a narrowing on the same predicate module as #29023 (`packages/spec/src/ui/duplicate-global-filter-names.ts`, after PR #29162 merges). Also read whether a `dateRange` entry is meaningful at all when the dashboard does NOT declare `dateRange`.

Reader who acts: `domain:spec`.

Dedupe: searched `reserved dateRange global filter name`, `globalFilters dateRange collision`, `dashboard reserved filter name`. Only #29023 and its PR. **New.**
